tasks.title: Initialize Project Structure and Dependencies
tasks.description: Set up the Node.js project with TypeScript, install required dependencies, and configure build tooling for the MCP server.
tasks.details:
1. Initialize npm project:
   ```bash
   npm init -y
   ```

2. Install production dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install @modelcontextprotocol/sdk zod
   ```

3. Install dev dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install -D typescript @types/node vitest
   ```

4. Create tsconfig.json with strict mode:
   ```json
   {
     "compilerOptions": {
       "target": "ES2022",
       "module": "NodeNext",
       "moduleResolution": "NodeNext",
       "strict": true,
       "esModuleInterop": true,
       "skipLibCheck": true,
       "outDir": "./dist",
       "rootDir": "./src",
       "declaration": true,
       "resolveJsonModule": true
     },
     "include": ["src/**/*"],
     "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "tests"]
   }
   ```

5. Update package.json scripts:
   ```json
   {
     "type": "module",
     "main": "dist/index.js",
     "scripts": {
       "build": "tsc",
       "start": "node dist/index.js",
       "dev": "tsc --watch",
       "test": "vitest",
       "test:e2e": "vitest run tests/e2e"
     }
   }
   ```

6. Create directory structure:
   - src/
   - src/tools/
   - tests/
   - tests/e2e/

7. Update .env.example with ProcurementExpress variables:
   ```
   PE_API_BASE_URL=https://api.procurementexpress.com
   PE_CLIENT_ID=your_client_id
   PE_CLIENT_SECRET=your_client_secret
   ```

8. Update .gitignore to include dist/
tasks.testStrategy: Verify setup by running: npm install (no errors), npm run build (compiles successfully), npm test (vitest runs). Check that tsconfig.json strict mode catches type errors. Ensure all directories exist and package.json has correct scripts.

subtasks.title: Implement ApiClient class with HTTP methods and header injection
subtasks.description: Create src/api-client.ts with the ApiClient class that handles all HTTP requests, authentication headers, and company ID injection.
subtasks.details:
Implement the ApiClient class in src/api-client.ts:

1. Class structure:
   - Private properties: baseUrl: string, token: string | null, companyId: string | null
   - Constructor accepting baseUrl parameter

2. Token and company management:
   - setToken(token: string): void - stores bearer token
   - setCompanyId(companyId: string): void - stores company ID for header
   - getToken(): string | null - retrieves current token (for validation)
   - clearAuth(): void - clears both token and companyId (for logout)

3. Header injection (private getHeaders method):
   - Always include 'Content-Type': 'application/json'
   - Add 'Authorization': `Bearer ${token}` when token is set
   - Add 'app_company_id': companyId when companyId is set

4. Core request method:
   - async request<T>(method: string, path: string, body?: unknown): Promise<T>
   - Construct full URL: `${baseUrl}${path}`
   - Use native fetch with method, headers, and JSON-stringified body
   - Handle non-ok responses by throwing ApiClientError
   - Parse and return JSON response typed as T

5. HTTP convenience methods (all call request internally):
   - get<T>(path: string): Promise<T>
   - post<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T>
   - put<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T>
   - patch<T>(path: string, body: unknown): Promise<T>
   - delete<T>(path: string): Promise<T>

Use ES module syntax with .js extensions in imports. Export the ApiClient class as a named export.
subtasks.testStrategy:
Unit test ApiClient methods using mocked fetch (vi.mock('node:fetch') or global.fetch mock). Test cases:
1. Verify headers include Content-Type always
2. Verify Authorization header added when token is set
3. Verify app_company_id header added when companyId is set
4. Verify headers work correctly with both, one, or neither auth values
5. Test each HTTP verb method calls request with correct method string
6. Verify body is JSON-stringified for POST/PUT/PATCH
7. Verify GET/DELETE don't include body

subtasks.title: Implement ApiClientError class and error handling unit tests
subtasks.description: Create the ApiClientError custom error class and comprehensive unit tests for error handling across HTTP status codes 400, 401, 403, 404, and 500.
subtasks.details:
1. Implement ApiClientError class in src/api-client.ts:
   - Extend Error base class
   - Constructor parameters: statusCode: number, message: string, errors?: Record<string, string[]>
   - Set this.name = 'ApiClientError'
   - Store statusCode and errors as public properties
   - Call super(message) to set error message

2. Update ApiClient.request() error handling:
   - Check response.ok, if false handle error
   - Try to parse error response body as JSON
   - Extract message from error.message or use default 'API request failed'
   - Extract errors object from error.errors if present
   - Throw new ApiClientError(response.status, message, errors)
   - Handle JSON parse failures gracefully (use empty object)

3. Create unit tests in tests/api-client.test.ts:
   - Test ApiClientError construction preserves all properties
   - Test instanceof Error returns true
   - Test error.name equals 'ApiClientError'

4. Test error handling scenarios:
   - 400 Bad Request: Returns validation errors in errors property
   - 401 Unauthorized: Token invalid or missing
   - 403 Forbidden: User lacks permission
   - 404 Not Found: Resource doesn't exist
   - 500 Internal Server Error: Server-side failure
   - Malformed JSON response: Graceful handling with default message

Ensure all tests use mocked fetch to simulate API responses. Use Vitest describe/it/expect syntax.
subtasks.testStrategy:

1. Mock global.fetch for all tests

subtasks.description: Implement src/auth.ts containing the AuthManager class that handles OAuth2 password grant authentication, token validation, and token revocation.
subtasks.details:
Create src/auth.ts with the AuthManager class:

2. Implement AuthManager class:
   - Private properties: apiClient (ApiClient), clientId, clientSecret, currentToken (string | null)
   - Constructor accepting ApiClient, clientId, clientSecret parameters

3. Implement authenticate(email, password) method:
   - POST to /oauth/token with grant_type='password', email, password, client_id, client_secret
   - Store access_token in currentToken
   - Call apiClient.setToken() to configure subsequent requests
   - Return the access token

4. Implement validateToken() method:
   - Return false if no currentToken exists

5. Implement revokeToken() method:
   - Skip if no currentToken
   - POST to /oauth/revoke with the current token
   - Clear currentToken and reset apiClient token

6. Implement getToken() method returning currentToken

subtasks.title: Integrate auth tools into src/index.ts with MCP request handlers
subtasks.description: Register authentication tools in the main MCP server by importing auth tools, setting up ListToolsRequestSchema handler to expose available tools, and CallToolRequestSchema handler to route tool calls to appropriate handlers with error handling and JSON response formatting.
subtasks.details:
1. Import authToolDefinitions and createAuthToolHandlers from './tools/auth.js'
2. Initialize auth handlers by calling createAuthToolHandlers(authManager, apiClient)
3. Register ListToolsRequestSchema handler:
   - Return { tools: [...authToolDefinitions] } to expose auth tools
4. Register CallToolRequestSchema handler:
   - Extract name and arguments from request.params
   - Implement switch statement for tool routing:
     - 'authenticate': call authHandlers.authenticate(args)
     - 'validate_token': call authHandlers.validate_token()
     - 'revoke_token': call authHandlers.revoke_token()
     - default: throw Error('Unknown tool: ${name}')
   - Wrap handler results in MCP response format: { content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify(result) }] }
   - Implement try/catch for error handling: return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: JSON.stringify({ error: error.message }) }], isError: true }
